statement_text: Systolic blood pressure was reduced by 12 mmHg after 6 months of treatment with an ACE inhibitor in a cohort of 1,245 adults with hypertension.

variables.name: systolic blood pressure
variables.condition: after 6 months of ACE inhibitor treatment

evidence_span: systolic blood pressure was reduced by 12 mmHg after 6 months of treatment with an ACE inhibitor

statement_text: The reduction in systolic blood pressure was greater in patients with baseline systolic blood pressure >150 mmHg (mean reduction of 18 mmHg) compared to those with baseline systolic blood pressure 140-150 mmHg (mean reduction of 9 mmHg).
conditions: after 6 months of ACE inhibitor treatment
expected_value_or_relationship: Greater reduction in systolic blood pressure for higher baseline values
evidence_span: The reduction was greater in patients with baseline systolic blood pressure greater than 150 mmHg (mean reduction of 18 mmHg) compared to those with baseline systolic blood pressure between 140 and 150 mmHg (mean reduction of 9 mmHg).

statement_text: No significant difference in response to ACE inhibitor treatment was observed between male and female patients.
evidence_span: No significant difference in response was observed between male and female patients.
